analysis: Examined the four changed files in the provider-swift add-on hold and Autopilot paths. ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:207 now also cancels the selected-model recovery attempt when a hold begins. This tightens T-059/A-018 by stopping a recovery load from fighting the hold; the existing load fence (addonHoldLoadRefusal) and the settle loop are unchanged. ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:22 adds an in-progress selected-model recovery to the `.preload` busy reason. It makes the provider report busy and reject new Autopilot commands during recovery. This is fail-safe and affects only availability reporting. ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:213 calls noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command) after each successful eviction. ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:76 mirrors config.backend.enabledModels into savedEnabledModels on each settings refresh. Neither the definitions of these helpers nor the selectedModelRecovery and savedEnabledModels state are in the supplied evidence. The recovery logic is therefore unverified: whether noteSelectedModelUnloaded stops recovery from reloading models an Autopilot or operator unload removed, whether savedEnabledModels widens what is served beyond Autopilot consent (autopilotAllowsModel, ordinaryServingModelIDs), and whether recovery respects the privateOnly and consent gates. savedEnabledModels is read from the operator's own config file, which is the same trust domain as existing settings, so I found no concrete regression. No change to the wire protocol, App Attest, attestation, encryption or the hold socket peer checks (TB-012) is visible. The next pass should inspect the selectedModelRecovery implementation, noteSelectedModelUnloaded and savedEnabledModels consumers. In particular it should confirm that recovery cannot load models during a hold, a load via ensureModelLoaded with the addonHoldLoadRefusal check, or while an Autopilot command is active.
